objective: Resolve as many known issues as practical before v0.3.0 while preserving scientific correctness, backward-readable checkpoints, stable public contracts, Control interoperability, and fail-closed behavior.

execution_policy.new_feature_rule: Do not expand public geometry, boundary, lifting, or model combinations before S-03 through S-09 are closed, except for work strictly required to fix a registered issue.
execution_policy.threshold_rule: Do not relax a numerical, scientific, restart, memory, or performance threshold and do not add skip or xfail to obtain closure.
execution_policy.new_finding_rule: Every finding discovered before freeze must be fixed, verified, accepted by a confirmed decision, or explicitly deferred by a confirmed decision. No untriaged finding may remain.

requirements: PSSolver-Control uses only documented public PSSolver APIs.
Any provider-identity or metadata change has an explicit migration record.
Periodic and Channel installed-wheel CPU consumer suites pass.
The consolidated S-09 GPU/H100 qualification covers the Control paths affected by v0.3 changes.
No production default or functional API version changes implicitly.

completion_gates.title: Registry closure
completion_gates.criterion: All S-03 through S-09 issue IDs are verified or closed by independent evidence; S-10 items have a confirmed user decision; no untriaged issue remains.

completion_gates.title: Public error and metadata contract
completion_gates.criterion: Public execution, restart, checkpoint, and convergence failures use documented exception families and finite serializable metadata without stale running state.

completion_gates.title: Checkpoint compatibility and integrity
completion_gates.criterion: Released v0.2 fixtures remain readable; continuous/restart equivalence passes; NFS fallback, concurrency, tamper, permission, and failure-injection gates pass without residue or partial publication.

completion_gates.title: Numerical and scientific correctness
completion_gates.criterion: Finite-state, pressure residual, transform-count, Hermitian, gradient, Taylor, restart, and deterministic replay gates pass without relaxed thresholds.

completion_gates.title: CPU and packaging closure
completion_gates.criterion: Clean source and installed-wheel CPU suites pass; wheel/sdist contents, public imports, console entry points, fixture identities, and documentation bindings are verified.

completion_gates.title: Performance and memory non-regression
completion_gates.criterion: A pre-registered paired qualification on representative Plane, Periodic, and Channel paths passes the last accepted platform-specific runtime and memory limits.

completion_gates.title: Control interoperability
completion_gates.criterion: The independently versioned Control consumer passes installed-wheel CPU qualification and the affected GPU/H100 paths without private imports, hidden fallback, or identity ambiguity.

completion_gates.title: Consolidated GPU/H100 qualification
completion_gates.criterion: S-09 covers CUDA t>=200 Hermitian consistency, TF32 backward scope, CUDA-only tests, checkpoint/restart, gradients, memory, and non-regression in one pre-registered campaign, subject to user authorization.

completion_gates.title: Independent acceptance and release
completion_gates.criterion: A release candidate passes independent read-only acceptance, online asset identity checks, and post-release verification before v0.3.0 is declared complete.

decision_questions.question: Should known-issue closure take priority over new public features until S-09 is complete?
decision_questions.recommendation: Choose A. It minimizes moving interfaces while correctness, checkpoint, and compatibility debt is being removed.

options.A: Issue-first: no unrelated public features before S-09.
options.B: Allow narrowly scoped new features after S-04 when they do not change the active qualification surface.
options.C: Develop new features in parallel with all issue batches.

decision_questions.question: Should S-05 introduce a digest-protected checkpoint schema in v0.3.0?
decision_questions.recommendation: Choose A. Coordinated progress tampering cannot be fixed without authenticated progress metadata, and 0.3 is the appropriate compatibility boundary.

options.A: Yes: write the new digest-protected schema while retaining explicit read-only compatibility for released v0.2 checkpoints.
options.B: Add an opt-in upgraded schema but keep the old schema as the default writer for 0.3.0.

decision_questions.question: How strict should v0.3.0 performance and memory qualification be?
decision_questions.recommendation: Choose A. Reusing accepted platform-specific limits prevents silent regressions without inventing stricter thresholds after implementation.

options.A: Pre-register and reuse the last accepted representative-path runtime and memory limits; changes require a separate scientific justification and user decision.
options.B: Require byte-identical performance metrics or no measurable slowdown.
options.C: Treat performance and memory as informational only.

decision_questions.question: Should PSSolver-Control compatibility be a v0.3.0 release gate?
decision_questions.recommendation: Choose A. Control is an independent consumer of the stable functional API, so it is the strongest practical boundary test without coupling the repositories.

options.A: Yes: require installed-wheel CPU and affected S-09 GPU/H100 consumer qualification.
options.B: Require installed-wheel CPU qualification only; defer GPU consumer qualification.
options.C: Do not gate PSSolver v0.3.0 on the independent Control consumer.

decision_questions.question: What backward-compatibility promise should v0.3.0 make for checkpoints and provider identity?
decision_questions.recommendation: Choose A. It protects existing simulation data while allowing a safer v0.3 writer and keeps identity changes auditable.

options.A: Read all authenticated released v0.2 fixtures, never mutate sources, require restart equivalence, and require explicit migrations for identity changes.
options.B: Support only v0.2.2 fixtures and later.
options.C: Make v0.3 checkpoints intentionally incompatible with v0.2.

decision_questions.question: What default position should S-10 take on the three D-0007 items?
decision_questions.recommendation: Choose A. It addresses architectural debt when the correctness surface is stable, without reopening unqualified lifting physics or redesigning an accepted label contract prematurely.

options.A: After S-09, scope R1-R9 into a final 0.3 cleanup step if independently testable; keep B8/S2-07 deferred until lifting is deliberately reopened; keep A2-11 accepted.
options.B: Resolve R1-R9, B8/S2-07, and A2-11 all within v0.3.0.
options.C: Preserve D-0007 unchanged and leave all three outside v0.3.0.

decision_questions.question: What release sequence should close v0.3.0?
decision_questions.recommendation: Choose A. One frozen release candidate plus independent acceptance gives a clear evidence boundary while avoiding an unnecessary series of candidates.

options.A: Freeze v0.3.0rc1 after S-03 through S-10, run independent acceptance, then publish v0.3.0 only if no release-blocking finding appears.
options.B: Publish v0.3.0 directly after the internal qualification campaign.
options.C: Plan multiple release candidates regardless of findings.
